sentences.text: Avalonianus is considered a dubious or invalid genus of archosaur from the Late Triassic Westbury Formation of England.
The genus was originally described by Harry Seeley in 1898.
The name was later renamed by Oskar Kuhn in 1961 because the original name was preoccupied.
The type species for the genus is Avalonia sanfordi.
Subsequent analyses demonstrated that the remains were a paleontological chimera of Camelotia material and teeth from an archosaur or a possible primitive theropod.
The genus is classified within the parent group Saurischia.
